item1.justification: The trace applies element-by-element anticipation under §102, expressly addresses the Graham/KSR considerations under §103, and compares the disputed claim language with the specification under §112, notwithstanding some doctrinal imprecision in its §112(f) treatment.

item2.justification: The conclusions are tied to specific limitations such as “minimum three pairs of crossed legs,” “connecting hardware,” and “tabletop,” as well as disclosures in US-2012318946-A1 and identified specification examples.

item3.justification: The office action and final decision consistently preserve the earlier novelty and nonobviousness findings while rejecting solely on the separately identified §112 deficiencies.

item4.justification: The broad interpretation of “connecting hardware” and “minimum three pairs of crossed legs,” followed by rejection of their ambiguous scope, reasonably reflects the profile’s high claim-breadth setting and moderate strictness.

item5.justification: The final rejection directly follows the office action’s §112 grounds and expressly explains why those grounds preclude allowance despite favorable §102 and §103 findings.
